raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Clients built on the Anthropic Messages API (the anthropic SDK, Claude Code) cannot use sgl-router today: it only serves chat completions. This adds `POST /v1/messages` and `POST /v1/messages/count_tokens` to the router.

## Modifications

A Messages request is converted to a chat request at ingress and served by the existing `chat_completions` handler, so it is routed exactly like chat (tokenization, cache-aware routing, admission, retry, PD). The reply is converted back on the outer body, streaming or not.

- **Request**: `system` as a string or text blocks; content as a string or blocks; text and image (base64 / url) blocks; `tool_use` / `tool_result` round trips; assistant thinking history sent as `reasoning_content`.
- **Parameters**: `thinking` → `chat_template_kwargs`, `output_config.effort` → `reasoning_effort` (unchanged), `output_config.format` / `output_format` → `response_format`, `stop_sequences` as a string or array, `top_k` passed through. Conversion works on `serde_json::Value`, so sglang chat extensions pass through.
- **Reply**: `thinking`, `text` and `tool_use` blocks; `stop_reason` covers `end_turn` / `max_tokens` / `tool_use` / `stop_sequence`; usage includes `cache_read_input_tokens`.
- **Streaming**: the spec event sequence (`message_start` → block start / delta / stop → `message_delta` → `message_stop`). Continuous usage is enabled so `message_start` carries `input_tokens`.
- **count_tokens**: answered by the router's own chat encoder, without an engine call; 400 when the model's tokenizer is disabled.
- **Errors**: every non-2xx answer uses the Anthropic `{"type": "error", "error": {...}}` envelope with the type for its status: router rejections, engine errors, in-stream errors and the body-limit 413.
- `src/protocol/sse.rs` is a small generic layer that rewrites a chat SSE body into another protocol's events (`SseTransducer`, `transduce_body`). It wraps the body produced by `proxy/sse.rs`, so timeouts, abort-on-disconnect and TTFT/ITL metrics are unchanged.

The companion PR for OpenAI `/v1/responses` (#42314) carries a byte-identical `protocol/sse.rs`; whichever lands second only needs a one-line rebase in `protocol/mod.rs`.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A: no model or kernel change.

Unit tests cover conversion, buffered and streamed replies and error envelopes; `tests/proxy/messages_api.rs` drives requests end to end through a mock worker. `cargo test` (lib + proxy) and `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` pass.

Also validated against a live deployment: the official anthropic Python SDK's types, and Claude Code pointed at the router (tool use, streaming, multi-turn, images, subagents).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A: no change to the chat path.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

nodes.body:
[P2] Tool blocks are keyed by `(kind, index)`, which breaks in two ways:

1. **Separate calls merge.** SGLang's Gemma 4 parser reuses the index for separate calls to the same tool. Two weather calls merge into one block with invalid arguments: `{"city":"Paris"}{"city":"Rome"}`.
2. **One call splits.** Any text or reasoning delta in the middle of a call closes the block. Feeding idx0 `{"x":` → text `"\n"` → idx0 `1}` gives `tool_use{name: f}` with `{"x":`, then a text block, then `tool_use{id: toolu_<random>, name: ""}` with `1}`.

Suggest: a chunk carrying `function.name` (SGLang sends it only on a call's first chunk) always starts a new tool block; argument-only chunks go to the open tool block; text that arrives mid-call is held back (or dropped if it is only whitespace).

[P2] Please set `continue_final_message` when the request ends with an assistant prefix. The Messages API expects the reply to continue that prefix, but without the flag both the router's formatter and the engine turn it into a user message. For example, a final assistant message containing `{"answer":` becomes user content instead of the start of the answer.

[P2] `request_tokens_for` falls back to counting raw text when chat rendering fails, so `count_tokens` returns 200 with a count that leaves out template and tool overhead.

Please call `encode_chat` directly and return an error on failure. Also note that image tokens are not counted.
The SSE scanner also accepts `{"error": "queue full"}` (a string). Here that becomes `"upstream error"`. Adding an `err.as_str()` fallback keeps the message.

Small conversion issues:
- Multiple assistant `text` blocks are joined with no separator, and their order relative to `tool_use` is lost (L339).
- A `tool_result` with several content blocks loses `is_error`; only string content (or a single text block, which is collapsed) gets the "Error: " prefix (L310).
- A user turn with `content: []` is dropped, which can leave two assistant turns in a row.
Nit: the two route blocks are identical apart from the handler. A small helper would remove the duplication.

Nit: a few inputs are accepted beyond the spec:
- string `stop_sequences`
- `system` role inside `messages`
- an `id` fallback for `tool_use_id`
- `image_url` passthrough

Each adds surface area and tests. Unless a client needs one, could we drop them to keep this smaller?

[P2] Consecutive same-role turns are not merged. Each turn is converted on its own, so two user messages in a row stay separate, and templates that require alternating roles fail to render. The Messages API combines consecutive user or assistant turns into one ([docs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/messages/create)).

Please merge them before conversion, keeping `tool_result` blocks in order.

files.patch:
@@ -547,6 +547,27 @@ forwarded as sent, since the engine renders and tokenizes each query-document
 pair. Routing is on load, with each pair's size estimated from its text. As for
 embeddings, a PD fleet answers 400 and `--dp-aware` pins no rank.
 
+## Anthropic Messages
+
+`/v1/messages` converts each request to a chat completion at ingress, so it is
+routed exactly like `/v1/chat/completions`, and converts the reply (or stream)
+back to the Messages format. Consecutive turns of the same role are merged, as
+the Messages API does, and a final assistant turn is sent as a prefill
+(`continue_final_message`). Besides the Messages fields, only
+`chat_template_kwargs` and `continue_final_message` reach the chat request.
+Every error uses the Anthropic error envelope; 5xx messages are replaced with a
+generic one, and a failed stream still closes its open block and ends with
+`message_stop`.
+
+`/v1/messages/count_tokens` is answered by the router from the model's chat
+template, without calling an engine. Image tokens are not counted, and a model
+without a chat template answers 500 rather than a raw-text estimate.
+
+`thinking` sets the `thinking` / `enable_thinking` chat template kwargs. The
+engine's own `/v1/messages` also adapts it per reasoning parser (for example
+`reasoning_effort` for Hunyuan), which the router cannot see; on such models
+use `output_config.effort` or `chat_template_kwargs` directly.
+
 ## DeepSeek V4 and V4.1
 
 Native V4 and V4.1 rendering comes from `rust/sglang-processor`, shared with SGLang's Rust
